28 Which diagram shows the diffraction of water waves in a ripple tank?
A
B
C
D

hints: Notice the straight plane wavefronts on the left passing through a gap whose width is similar to the wavelength.
Recall that diffraction through a narrow gap spreads the wave into the shadow region while wavelength and speed stay the same in the same water depth.
Compare the four right-hand patterns for circular wavefronts centred at the gap with unchanged spacing between successive crests.
walkthrough: Identify the set-up: straight parallel crests approach a barrier with a small central gap, so the transmitted wave should show diffraction.
State the rule: when gap width is comparable to wavelength $\lambda$, the gap acts like a new source and wavefronts spread out as circular arcs into the region behind the barrier.
Check wavelength: diffraction does not change speed or frequency in the same ripple tank, so the spacing $\lambda$ of the crests must be the same on both sides of the barrier.
Eliminate A because there is almost no spreading, and eliminate D because the crest spacing grows larger on the right, and eliminate B because the curvature is not a full centred circular spread.
The pattern with centred circular arcs of unchanged spacing spreading widely behind the gap matches diffraction. This is option C.

A.explanation: Shows plane wavefronts passing through the narrow gap with no spreading into the shadow region, so diffraction is not shown.

B.explanation: Shows curved wavefronts but they are not centred on the gap and do not spread correctly into a wide circular pattern.

C.explanation: Shows plane waves passing through a narrow gap and spreading out as circular wavefronts with the same wavelength, which is diffraction.

D.explanation: Shows spreading but the spacing of the wavefronts on the right increases away from the gap, implying wavelength changes, which is incorrect for diffraction.
